note: Pairing word-code vectors. The code carries no integrity on its own; the six-digit SAS does. These vectors pin the codec and the S (invitation MAC key) derivation so the edge, the CLI and the Python verifier agree. The wordlist that generation draws from is a separate concern (licence pending); these vectors use fixed example words and do not require any word to be in the list.

codec.format: canonical code = nameplate + '-' + words joined by '-'; nameplate is the leading all-digit token; words are lowercase a-z.
codec.parse: split the input on runs of '-' and/or ASCII whitespace; trim; lowercase (NFKC); the first token (all digits) is the nameplate, the rest are the words. A leading/trailing separator is ignored. The parse is lenient on separators and case; generation always emits the canonical hyphen form.

s_derivation.ikm: utf8( NFKC( lowercase( words joined by one ASCII space ) ) )
s_derivation.salt: utf8( nameplate + '|' + invitation )   (invitation is the one-time invitation identity I's address, the 'ed25519:'+64hex string, named `invitation` on the wire to match the built edge/relay shape; both sides hold it: the inviter created I, the acceptor reads it from the relay claim; a '|' separator is REQUIRED, not bare concatenation)
s_derivation.output: S, the 16-byte invitation MAC key; the pairing request is MAC'd under S exactly as the existing peer ceremony
